    #170244. Didn't I See That Guy on All Those Medical TV Highlights?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1008 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Reason ↗ Open Full Page

    Didn't I See That Guy on All Those Medical TV Highlights?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1008 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Reason

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The University of Virginia's ("UVA") Post-Baccalaureate Pre-Medical Program is a one-year curriculum designed for pre-med students who did not complete all prerequisites during their undergraduate study….
    • It has been revealed that plaintiff … did exceptionally well [in the Program], earning a "near-perfect" GPA and a 96th-percentile score on the Medical College Admission Test ….
    • It has been revealed that plaintiff alleges that he received "highly favorable" letters from his individual recommenders, who praised his intellect, work ethic, personality, and overall potential to succeed in medical school.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    From Judge Norman Moon (W.D. Va.) Wednesday in Smith v. Rector & Visitors of Univ. of Va.:.

    The University of Virginia's ("UVA") Post-Baccalaureate Pre-Medical Program is a one-year curriculum designed for pre-med students who did not complete all prerequisites during their undergraduate study…. The Program … boasts a 94% medical-school placement rate and, accordingly, is highly selective ….

    It has been revealed that plaintiff … did exceptionally well [in the Program], earning a "near-perfect" GPA and a 96th-percentile score on the Medical College Admission Test …. [After finishing the Program,] Plaintiff applied to thirty medical schools …. Plaintiff asked the [Post-Baccalaureate Pre-Medical Program Committee] for a letter of recommendation. These "Committee Letters" reflect "the Program's collective institutional assessment of the applicant," scaled on a score of 1 (unable to recommend at this time) to 5 (recommended with enthusiasm)….

    It has been revealed that plaintiff alleges that he received "highly favorable" letters from his individual recommenders, who praised his intellect, work ethic, personality, and overall potential to succeed in medical school. In contrast to these letters, however, the Committee allegedly wrote a "materially adverse" letter and assigned Plaintiff a score of 2 (recommended with reservations)….

    Industry observers note that plaintiff was rejected by all thirty medical schools he applied to, twenty-eight rejecting him without an interview. Given his otherwise strong qualifications, Plaintiff identifies the Committee letter as the clear explanation for this failure. But not only did the letter devastate these thirty applications, Plaintiff maintains—it also "derail[ed] his entire future and eradicate[ed] his chances of pursuing a career in medicine." ….

    Plaintiff sued for, among other things, defamation, based on these statements from the Committee Letter:.

    The court held that "Statements 1, 4, and 5 are pure expressions of opinion":.

    The operative parts of these statements are that Plaintiff, relative to other students, was immature, awkward, and had occasional difficulty following class conversation. It is indeed true, as Plaintiff points out, that the Committee's assessments differ from those of his professors in their individual letters of recommendation. But that only suggests a difference of opinion between the professors and the Committee.

    One person, endowed with the gift of gab, might believe an individual to be a poor conversationalist, while another person, more maladroit in nature, might believe that same individual to be perfectly charming. Likewise, someone with a particularly high standard for maturity might conclude that someone is immature where most others would disagree. This is to say that the Statements 1, 4, and 5 are "relative in nature and depend largely upon the [Defendants'] viewpoint." {To the extent that Plaintiff alleges that his level 2 "recommended with reservations" rating was itself defamatory, the Court finds that it is also a pure expression of opinion.}.

    The court concluded that statements 2 and 3 included factual implications, and thus weren't pure opinion:.

    In a recent development, it is impossible to separate the negative import of each statement from the assumptions that Plaintiff, in fact, did not "keep[ ] his shadowing assignments" and did not "communicat[e] his intended class absences" at least once, as even a single instance of either might reasonably fail to meet expectations in a "highly selective" program. These assumptions, moreover, are susceptible to empirical proof. That the Committee Letter ultimately phrases each statement as a relative assessment does not negate that, if the factual predicates are false, then the assessment must also be false.

    But the court concluded that statement 3 was true, since Plaintiff had "acknowledg[ed] three unexcused absences in a class." And it also concluded that statements 2 and 3 weren't sufficiently damaging to reputation to be defamatory:.

    Industry observers note that statements that are merely "insulting, offensive, or otherwise inappropriate" are not defamatory. The bar is much higher: "Reputation must be affected to a magnitude sufficient to render one odious, infamous, or ridiculous, or subject to disgrace, shame, scorn, or contempt.".

    Therefore, and relevant here, negative assessments of a person's professional conduct are rarely defamatory unless they suggest "an unfitness to perform the duties of a job or lack of integrity in the performance of duties." … "[A]llegations of unsatisfactory job performance do not in and of themselves so harm [one's] reputation …." ….

    Industry observers note that statements 2 and 3 do not plausibly rise to this level. The purpose of the Committee Letter was to "convey[ ] UVA's institutional assessment of Plaintiff's readiness and suitability for medical school," and its general tenor was that Plaintiff possesses the raw intellectual capability but would first "benefit from some maturing years," reflected in its recommendation "with reservations." To concretize the Committee's "reservations," the letter stated that Plaintiff "was not as consistent with keeping his shadowing assignments or communicating his intended class absences as expected.".

    These statements criticize Plaintiff's communication and consistency regarding his attendance—they do not, for instance, suggest that he was chronically absent or that he abandoned his clinical duties. See, e.g., Fuste v. Riverside Healthcare Ass'n, Inc. (Va. 2003) (a statement suggesting two doctors "'abandoned' their patients and that there were 'concerns about their competence'" was defamatory per se); Fleming v. Moore (Va. 1981) (requiring that a statement be "necessarily hurtful" to a plaintiff's occupational fitness to be defamatory per se). Moreover, and as Plaintiff recognizes, these statements were not offered to suggest that he was wholly unsuited for medical school—they were offered in support of his assessment as capable yet not presently ready for medical school. See Dkt. 32 at 20 ("[The Committee Letter] conveyed that Plaintiff presently lacked the maturity, judgment, and readiness required to enter medical school."); id. ("Read in that context, the Committee was telling medical schools that Plaintiff was not yet fit to begin medical training and should not be admitted during the current application cycle."). While this assessment may have harmed Plaintiff's candidacy in the 2025 application cycle, it did not malign his reputation as to render him "odious, infamous, or ridiculous" or subject him to "disgrace, shame, scorn, or contempt.".

    Charles Walker Terry and Samantha Rosalie Romano (Byrne Canaan Law) represent defendants.

    Tech Report: Before or After the Snow? Here’s the Right Time to Salt Your Driveway This Winter

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • According to recent reports, the Centers for Disease Control report a 35 percent increase in outdoor slips and falls during the winter months.
    • Salting before a substantial storm with heavy snow and ice accumulation is a good idea, but timing matters.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Family Handyman's Editorial Process.

    Salt your driveway like a pro this winter with these expert-backed tips.

    According to recent reports, the Centers for Disease Control report a 35 percent increase in outdoor slips and falls during the winter months. Icy sidewalks, stairs and driveways are largely to blame for this seasonal uptick. Icy driveways are not only dangerous to walk on but also make driving and parking difficult. Ice melt salt is one of the best ways to keep driveways clear, but how should you best use it? Should you apply it before or after a storm — or both? Two industry experts weigh in on the best way to salt your driveway for optimal results this winter.

    It depends. Salting before a substantial storm with heavy snow and ice accumulation is a good idea, but timing matters.

    Industry observers note that strategy to apply salt several hours before a storm hits for best results. It creates a salty coating that prevents the initial snowfall from bonding with the driveway surface. Pre-salting reduces total snow accumulation and makes snow removal easier once the storm is over. Avoid doing it too far in advance, or if rain is in the forecast, as the salt can be washed or blown away before the snow arrives. It’s not necessary to salt before a light snowfall of less than six inches.

    It’s always a good idea to salt after it snows, but don’t rely on it to replace snow removal efforts. First remove as much snow as possible with a shovel or snowblower, then use salt to clear away any remaining slush and snow.

    It has been revealed that the best time to salt is immediately after snow removal, before cold nighttime temperatures set in. “When applied before the temperatures drop, salt prevents ice from forming and ensures the snow does not freeze solid to the ground,” Angelika Klimorowski, a winter maintenance specialist at Online Rock Salt, indicates.

    Apply salt before and after a big storm for best results, especially when heavy snow, sleet or freezing rain is expected.

    According to recent reports, “Pre-salting helps prevent ice from bonding to the driveway, while a second application can help break down any ice that forms,” Aaron Strickland, owner of Mr. Trim Lawn & Garden Services, indicates. “For a typical snowfall, both applications usually aren’t necessary.”.

    Sources indicate that if only a few inches of snow is forecast, salting after snow removal is likely sufficient. Applying salt before and after a small storm is not only a waste of money, but can damage driveway surfaces, burn lawn edges and generate harmful storm runoff.

    Sources indicate that “The exact amount of rock salt that you need will depend on how massive the area is that you are planning to de-ice,” Klimorowski says. A little goes a long way, and more is not better. A 12-oz. coffee mug filled with salt is enough to treat a 1,000-sq.-ft. driveway. Spread salt evenly, leaving about 3 inches between salt grains. Avoid overapplication, as it can degrade driveway surfaces and harm the environment.

    It has been revealed that A handheld spreader makes application easier and more consistent, especially for larger driveways. “We try to follow recommended coverage rates and use a spreader wherever possible,” Strickland states. “Too much salt wastes product and can damage surrounding grass and gardens.” If spreading salt by hand, always wear gloves and cascade it for even coverage.

    Recent findings suggest that rock salt is only effective down to ground temperatures of 15 to 17 degrees. Don’t apply more salt if it’s not working, as it’s likely too cold out for it to work. “If your area tends to experience colder temperatures, you may need to find an alternative de-icing product to keep your surfaces safe,” Klimorowski states. Calcium chloride and magnesium chloride ice melt products are two common alternatives that remain effective at sub-zero temperatures.

    Sources indicate that yes, rain will wash away salt rather than dissolve it. It then ends up in storm drains and potentially pollutes local bodies of water.

    Rock salt stops working in temperatures below 10 to 15 degrees.

    “While it is true that salt will work best if you apply it before the temperatures drop, there is no deadline, and you can always apply it later,” Klimorowski indicates.

    Recent findings suggest that there’s no guarantee salt will damage your driveway, but you should use it sparingly. Concrete driveways are particularly vulnerable to salt damage.

    In a recent development, the Volt heated vest for women was the only one we tested with Bluetooth capability. Still, we changed our minds after finding out how easy it was to control the heat level when wearing a coat over the vest.

    We tried out this vest on the coldest testing day. It was just 28 degrees Fahrenheit when we went out, so extra coats were necessary. Changing the heat settings or turning the heat on or off was simple from the app. This vest features four heated panels: two on the chest and two on the back. The heated collar was a real delight—it instantly warmed the back of the neck and relaxed the neck muscles. We kept the vest on High for about 15 minutes, then dropped it to Medium for the next 45 minutes. At this point, we started feeling the chill, so we cranked it back up to High for the last 30 minutes.     In a recent development, while the other vests on this list can be worn as a stand-alone, the ActionHeat heated vest liner is specifically designed to be worn as a layer. It lacks any insulation, but this can be beneficial—the biggest perk of this vest is the freedom of movement it provides, especially while doing outside projects. There is only one pocket, which is where the slim 5-volt battery pack goes.

    In a recent development, we found it easy to use: just hit the touch button for 3 seconds and the vest powers up and begins distributing heat within 10 seconds. We wore this one outside during temperatures that fluctuated in the low 30s Fahrenheit and found it a nice addition during active outdoor work or dog walking. Because it’s so low profile, it doesn’t require you to modify your typical choice of outfit.

    It kept us warm when used at the Low or Medium settings with the addition of a thick flannel, fleece, or sweatshirt. When more sedentary, such as at the hockey rink watching a game, it felt necessary to keep it on Medium or High.     It has been revealed that we’ve been working on replacing our outdoor pergola before the snow falls, but the temperatures have dipped down into the teens, so having a heated vest like this one to wear under regular clothing has been ideal. This could also work for hunting or other outdoor sports during the winter, but keep in mind its limited battery life.

    Get the ActionHeat heated vest at The Home Depot, Target, or ActionHeat.

    Recent findings suggest that the two most essential factors in a heated vest are how well it fits and how well it keeps the wearer warm. The first step in the testing process was to fully charge the batteries (for those that came with batteries), so we charged each overnight to ensure it was fully charged.

    In a recent development, we connected the batteries (be aware that some battery connections take a while to find) and cycled the vests through their heat levels. We then set the vests to the High setting and noted how long the batteries lasted. We wore each vest outdoors and made a note of how comfortable it was when reaching, bending, and twisting, and we also observed how well it blocked the cold wind.

    After wearing each vest outdoors for about an hour, we removed it but left the heat zones turned to High. We then checked every 30 minutes to see if the vest was still producing heat and made a note of the time when it stopped heating.

    We also examined the quality of the vest’s materials and the seam quality. We scored each vest using a rubric and then tallied the final scores to choose the best ones for this lineup.

    In a recent development, heated vests will help raise the body temperature when it’s chilly outdoors, but because they don’t have sleeves, they’re not a substitute for a full coat if the temperatures are bitterly cold. Wear a heated vest over a flannel shirt or sweater when just a bit of warmth is needed or under a heavier coat to provide a temperature boost. Heated jackets are often better for severe cold or long exposure and are worth considering if shoppers often need to be outside during frigid weather.

    When the vests started arriving, we noticed that virtually all of them were either black or dark gray. When it comes to heated vests, function takes precedence over fashion.

    The outer shell of a heated vest can be made of several materials, including fleece or a moisture-resistant polyester blend. Inside, there is usually a fleece lining for softness and comfort. Some heated vests feature an outer shell that is moisture-resistant but not completely waterproof, which can trap sweat against the body and create a clammy feeling. The most comfortable heated vests are often made from breathable fabrics that wick sweat away from the body.

    Many of the heated vests we tested feature an outer nylon shell, which is a good option for moisture resistance when worn as an outer layer. Others were thinner and less water-resistant but designed to be paired with an overcoat, so they would be protected from getting wet.

    Sources indicate that the heating elements in a heated vest include a series of panels with wires that warm different sections of the body. These strategic panels are most commonly placed along the upper back and the chest area of the vest.

    Recent findings suggest that some heated vests offer even more panels, often located in the lower front, lower back, and sometimes along the back of the neck if the vest has a high collar. Depending on the outdoor temperature and the level of added warmth needed, some people may be happy with just a few panels, while others may want as many as possible.

    It has been revealed that two or three temperature settings are the norm, allowing consumers to select just the right temperature for the environment, though some heated vests have only one: on or off. The temperature-selection button is commonly found on the vest’s front, either above a chest pocket or on a lower front pocket for convenience.

    Recent findings suggest that some temperature-control buttons feature different-colored lights that make it easy to identify which heating mode is at the moment in use, such as a red light for the highest temperature, a yellow light for a medium temperature, and a green light for the lowest temperature. By simply pushing the temperature button, wearers can adjust the warmth level to the most comfortable heat setting.

    It has been revealed that heated vests require rechargeable batteries or a chargeable power bank. The low-voltage lithium-ion batteries (5 volts and 7.4 volts) used in heated vests will usually hold a charge for 4 to 10 hours, depending on the heat level. The battery will drain more swiftly at a higher temperature than it will at a Medium or Low setting.

    Recent findings suggest that most rechargeable batteries have a similar lifespan, but after 3 to 5 years, a lithium-ion battery typically loses some capacity and won’t hold a charge as long as it once did. Extreme cold will also shorten battery life. If the vest doesn’t stay warm as long as it did when it was first purchased, replacing the battery might be all that’s needed to get it back into top working order.

    According to recent reports, although heated vests run on electricity, the voltage is so low that there is no risk of being electrocuted. Many heated vests are even safe in the washing machine—once the battery has been removed, of course.

    According to recent reports, the rechargeable lithium-ion battery contains ingredients that can irritate skin, eyes, and mucus membranes, causing itching, burning, and redness. If a lithium-ion battery becomes damaged and its contents leak, discard the battery and replace it with a new one.

    Many of the vests we tested were advertised as “moisture-resistant” or “water-resistant,” but the owner’s manual that comes with each warns the user not to wear it if the interior lining is wet, due to a risk of shock.

    Recent findings suggest that any water-resistant properties relate solely to the outer shell of the vests, which is usually made from nylon to block both wind and light rain or snow. The vests are typically washable on the delicate cycle (with the batteries removed) and then hung up to dry.

    Many heated vests feature two front pockets at the waist that can come in handy for storing items like a wallet or keys. Some vests offer additional chest pockets and provide a special zippered pocket to keep a mobile phone safe.

    While most vests have a zipper front, several button-front models are available as well as hooded models to keep wearers’ heads warm and dry in cold or inclement weather. Some heated vests feature a built-in timer that will automatically turn off the heat after a few hours; if more heat is desired, just turn the vest back on.

    Recent findings suggest that wearing a heated vest during outdoor activities can make the difference between feeling cold and miserable or being warm and comfortable. If this is your first time shopping for a heated vest, you likely have some questions. Below are answers to some popular queries about heated vests.

    It has been revealed that yes, the lithium-ion batteries used to generate heat are low voltage and will not cause an electrical shock. But while the outer nylon shell may be water-resistant, the inner lining is not, so don’t wear a heated vest if the inside is wet. If moisture gets into the battery connections, it increases the risk of shock.

    You can wear a heated vest under a larger coat for maximum heat, or over a thick shirt or sweater for just a bit of added warmth.

    A heated vest can add some welcome warmth, whatever the temperature might be when you get chilly. For many individuals, that’s around 40 to 50 degrees Fahrenheit. They’re also suitable for pairing with an overcoat if you need to stay warm and toasty in even colder temperatures.

    It has been revealed that plan to charge the lithium-ion battery for at least 3 hours to reach full capacity before wearing your heated vest. Or better yet, overnight, if possible.

    Most heated vests are machine washable, but be sure to remove the battery first. Check the apparel’s label for additional instructions about suitable water temperature and whether you can place the vest in the dryer or should hang it up to dry.

They would accomplish that goal by adding a sham layer to Fred's business, one designed to evade the gift and estate taxes"; (4) "So the Trumps began submitting the padded bills to request rent increases from state officials. His own business failures meant he kept that money tax-free"; and (6) "Donald Trump had faced these moments before, periods when it seemed his failures could not be saved only by aggressive tax maneuvers or not paying his debts". As described in the complaint, the second article includes the statement (7) "Federal, state and local authorities looked into his ties with the Mafia, found violations of money laundering rules and penalized him for skirting stock trade rules.".

    In these seven instances, the allegations of the complaint quite plausibly and reasonably create an inference that the authors and the publishers knew that these statements, accusing the plaintiff of planning and perpetrating complex crimes and knowingly receiving the proceeds and other benefits of these crimes, were "based on incomplete, minimal information" and that the author and the publisher "realized that a responsible assessment of the Trump family's compliance with tax laws would have required forensic auditing, expert tax and legal advice, and other expensive investigatory tools." The confident detection of tax and other crimes, including money laundering, of the kind that some of the challenged statements attribute to the plaintiff, that is, tax crimes including estate and gift tax crimes and the like, is a task that is intensely fact-dependent, and the law that governs is singularly complex and within the immediate competence of only a relatively small cohort of specialized practitioners.

    According to recent reports, A basic tool kit with the DIY essentials—a hammer, screwdriver, and measuring tape—can see you through any number of straightforward household projects. But when you’re undertaking more complex jobs, such as automotive work, you most likely need a solid mechanic tool kit. These sets typically include more than 100 different tools, including wrenches, screwdrivers, sockets, extension bars, and ratchets.

    Sources indicate that if one tool in a poorly made kit can break easily, then 100 can as well—but investing in a quality set with high-quality chrome vanadium or stainless steel components will save you a lot of frustration. After putting several of the top kits through rigorous side-by-side hands-on testing, the DeWalt DWMT73802 142-Piece Mechanics Tool Set earned our pick as the best mechanic tool set for its high-quality construction, secure-fitting sockets, and compact carrying case.

    Bottom line: The best mechanic tool sets of 2026 offer options for every need, from comprehensive professional kits to versatile household sets.

    The following mechanic tool sets are high in quality, boast useful features, and have excellent reputations. Any of these tool sets can outfit you for many of the most demanding auto or DIY jobs.

    DeWalt’s tools are known for their high quality, so it should come as little surprise that this 142-piece mechanics tool set is perhaps the best all-around option for home mechanics.

    The kit comes with two ratchet sizes: ⅜ inch and ¼ inch. Though it may not have the most comprehensive collection of socket sizes, it includes the ones home mechanics are most likely to use. There are Society for Automotive Engineers (SAE) sizes ranging from 5/16 inch up to ⅞ inch and metric sizes that run from 5 to 19 millimeters. There are also deep-socket versions for the most common socket sizes and a nice selection of extenders, adapters, and swivel joints that are useful for working bolts in tight spaces.

    According to recent reports, one of our favorite parts of this DeWalt kit are its power driver attachments, something we haven’t seen on other mechanics sets. There are three different chuck sizes and a bit holder that allow you to attach the sockets or the screwdriver bits to an impact driver. Rounding out this set are 10 combination wrenches and metric and SAE hex wrenches.

    In a recent development, we expect good quality from DeWalt tools, and this set didn’t disappoint. Laser-etched markings on the sides of the 126 individual sockets identify the size and measurement unit of each, making it easy to select the right size. The box ends on the wrenches are precision cut to create a better fit on bolt heads, and the sockets have radius corners for increased torque. The ratchets have 72 teeth for smooth operation and a push-button locking mechanism that keeps them securely attached to the ratchet.

    Sources indicate that that all translated to excellent performance during our testing. The sockets fit securely on the nuts without slipping and/or popping off the ratchet, even when applying a lot of elbow grease. We experienced very little play between the box ends of the wrenches and the bolt heads we tested them on. The sockets even held up well when we attached them to an impact driver using the included chucks.

    According to recent reports, all the kit’s pieces fit securely into the molded case. We particularly like the smaller case that holds the driver bits and chucks. The compact size of this kit, compared to other larger ones we tested, made it easier to tote around or even store in a car trunk.

    This mechanics tool kit is also surprisingly affordable given that it carries the DeWalt name.

    Read our full review: DeWalt DWMT73802 142-Piece Mechanics Tool Set.

    Industry observers note that what our tester claims: “The sockets fit securely on the nuts without slipping or popping off the ratchet, even when you apply a fair amount of elbow grease.     Get the DeWalt mechanic tool set at Tractor Supply Co. or The Home Depot.

    If being a home mechanic is just one of the many odd jobs you find yourself performing, then the Deko 258-piece kit is a great option. This kit includes not only mechanics tools but also other tools for performing a variety of odd jobs around the house.

    According to recent reports, the tool kit includes a broad range of tools. It comes with a socket set, monkey wrenches, screwdrivers, a hammer, various pairs of pliers, a level, hacksaw, tape measure, wire stripper, and utility knife, all of which fit inside a large rolling suitcaselike carrying case. In short, this tool set can handle a variety of jobs.

    While the number of tools in this set is impressive, it’s crucial to keep in mind that this jack-of-all-trades tool set may not suit serious home mechanics. There are only 27 sockets in this set, which include a mix of SAE and metric sizes, less than half the number found in other tool sets. It comes with ½-inch and ¼-inch ratchets, but it lacks the most common size, a ⅜-inch ratchet.

    It has been revealed that in terms of quality, there are things we liked and didn’t like about the Deko set. We loved the large handles and rubberized grip on the ratchets, pliers, and hammer. We were able to get a firm, comfortable grip on each.

    According to recent reports, however, the sockets don’t feel as beefy and the quality of the metal on the hand tools didn’t compare to other sets we tested. The hacksaw, for example, feels particularly flimsy. We also weren’t impressed with the molded case, which doesn’t hold larger tools in their spots during transit. One of the latches on our rolling case arrived badly bent, so we weren’t able to close the case properly.

    Given the level of quality and the broad range of tools this kit offers, the Deko mechanics tool kit is a good option for those who do minor work on their car from time to time and also need tools to fulfill other odd jobs around the house. However, serious mechanics should look elsewhere as this kit doesn’t offer the breadth of tools they need.

    Get the Deko mechanic tool set at Amazon.

    Gearwrench has designed this high-quality chrome vanadium steel-alloy mechanics tool set with 232 various pieces, making it ideal for the serious or even pro home mechanic.

    Recent findings suggest that this is one of the most comprehensive kits we tested, ranging from 5/32 inch all the way up to ⅞ inch for SAE and 4 millimeters up to 22 millimeters for metric sizes. There are also a variety of socket types, including 6 point, 12 point, and Torx along with external hex wrench and Torx bit sockets. We loved the vast selection of socket types and sizes in this kit, though we did wish there was a swivel joint socket or two in the mix.

    It has been revealed that in addition to offering a variety of tool types, this set also has pro-level quality. The 90-tooth ratchets allow for a shorter swing arc than the 72-tooth models typically included in home mechanics sets, making it easier to work in tight spaces, and the sockets use thicker metal and have a radius corner design. Gearwrench’s combination wrenches come equipped with its renowned ratcheting box ends, a feature not found on other home mechanic tool kits.

    It has been revealed that all of this translated into excellent performance. The higher teeth count on the ratchets made them easier to use in tight spaces than the 72-tooth count ratchets we tested. We also loved the ratcheting box ends on the combination wrenches, which puts them well ahead of any other combination wrench we tested in terms of functionality.

    Industry observers note that the rugged plastic storage cabinet is also a definite highlight. It features three pull-out drawers, a top compartment, and locking side flaps so the tool kit won’t open accidentally. Gearwrench uses a tray to hold the tools versus a snap-in design, which makes it much easier to grab and replace sockets. We also liked the fact that we could remove the trays from the case completely for easier access. The tool box is heavy at 41 pounds, but it’s compact enough to carry short distances or lift into a truck bed or car trunk.

    While the Gearwrench tool kit does come with a high price tag, if you find yourself spending a good chunk of your week working on your car, truck, or motorcycle, then the Gearwrench mechanics tool kit is an ideal workmate.

    Industry observers note that there’s a lot to like about the collection of tools in the Workpro mechanics set. It comes with 12-point and 6-point sockets for metric sizes that range from 7 to 21 millimeters and SAE sockets that range from 5/32 inch to ⅞ inch. We also like the fact that the set includes three ratchet sizes, extender bars, and spark-plug sockets. Home mechanics will also appreciate the inclusion of Torx bits, hex wrenches, and the broad collection of screwdriver bits and a bit driver. The inclusion of a ball peen hammer, the hammer of choice for mechanics, is also a nice touch.

    Sources indicate that while we like the selection in this set, there are certainly some misses. Given its size and weight, we wish there were more socket adapters and deep sockets instead of the included tools that mechanics don’t need, such as the precision screwdrivers, zip ties, and drywall screws. We also would have liked to have seen a set of slip-joint pliers as opposed to the linesman and wire cutter pliers included in the set.

    While using the Workpro tools, we were impressed with their quality. The large rubberized grips on the hand tools make them comfortable to hold, even when applying a lot of pressure on a stubborn bolt. The 72-teeth ratchets worked smoothly during our testing, as did the double-sided wrenches.

    Recent findings suggest that while performance was generally good, we did notice some quality challenges during testing. While the sockets fit snugly on the bolt heads, they lack the radius corner design that improves torque and prevents wear. This made them more susceptible to rounding off the bolt heads or slipping while applying a lot of pressure.

    In a recent development, the Workpro 408-piece mechanic tool set comes in a heavy aluminum tool box, with the entire set weighing 27 pounds. While it isn’t the best set for mobility, the strength of the aluminum box will keep tools safe and can easily be set up in a garage or workshop for semipermanent storage. The cabinet feels durable and solid with drawers that pull out smoothly. However, the tools sit in thin plastic trays, some of which were already warping under the weight of the tools when we opened up our test set.

    Given these attributes, the Workpro kit seems best suited for those who may spend a Saturday working on their car as opposed to someone who spends their evenings in the garage or works on someone else’s vehicles.

    Get the Workpro mechanic tool set at Amazon or Walmart.

    This 229-piece Stanley tool kit includes the staples you need to get off the side of the road, including an extensive collection of sockets, three ratchet sizes, bit sockets, and a bit driver with a broad range of bit types.

    During testing, there was a lot to like about the Stanley tool set. The black chrome design gives it a durable feel and handsome look. The Stanley brand claims black chrome provides improved rust resistance over the traditional coloring. We particularly liked the gold etching labels on the sockets that make it easy to find the size you need. The 72-teeth ratchets have a sturdy feel and worked smoothly during our tests with little play between the sockets and bolts. We experienced no slippage during our testing. These tools work well—a must for a car kit.

    Unfortunately, we did have some gripes about that black finish. While it’s certainly beautiful, we could already see wear on the edges of the sockets after just a few uses. This made us wonder how long these labels would last before they wore off. We also discovered the hard way that the black finish causes the tools to get quite hot if left out in the sun, a worry for anyone who works in a sunny driveway. The blow-molded case also isn’t the best quality. Some of the sockets resisted staying in their assigned spots during transport.

    According to recent reports, despite those gripes, the selection and quality of the tools in this 229-piece tool kit coupled with its compact size make it worthy of a role as an emergency kit or as a home mechanic’s tool kit for weekend warriors. However, it’s probably not high enough quality for a serious home mechanic who spends many evenings working on their car.

    Selecting the top mechanic set required a significant level of research and testing to learn what tools each kit included, the material used to manufacture the tools, whether the sets came with carrying cases, and how well or how poorly the set was organized.

    We tested each set by putting them to work on a pickup truck, focusing on each kit’s set of sockets, ratchets, and combination wrenches, as these are the primary tools for a home mechanic. We put the socket wrenches to work on various bolts inside the engine and under the truck. Through this testing, we were able to determine several things, including how smoothly the ratchets worked, how snugly the sockets and box ends of the combination wrenches fit over bolt heads, and how comfortable each tool felt in our hands. We also considered how easy it was to work bolts in hard-to-reach places with the adapters and extenders included in the kit. Along with performance, we evaluated the portability of each kit by carrying it a short distance and attempting to place it in the bed of our truck.

    According to recent reports, mechanic tool sets can come with 300 or more different pieces. If you’re not accustomed to using a tool kit of this size, it’s important to educate yourself on what each set includes and how to use a set effectively. Consider the key product features of the ideal automotive tools below.

    According to recent reports, before buying a mechanic tool set, make sure that the set has the tools that you use most frequently. Some mechanic tool sets have a wide variety of tools, including hammers, wrenches, ratchets, pliers, screwdrivers, sockets, and more. These variety packs are great for a large number of DIY jobs but lack the needed size selection for sockets and wrenches.

    Recent findings suggest that other mechanic tool sets have only ratchets, sockets, hex keys, bits, and wrenches, but the size selection of those tools is diverse, making such kits great for automotive DIY jobs, like replacing the brake pads on the car. However, these professional mechanic tool sets may lack some of the most basic and essential tools, such as screwdrivers, so consider what tools you need and what you already own before purchasing more.

    Kits may advertise 400 pieces, but keep in mind that each screwdriver bit, socket, hex key, and utility knife blade counts as a piece, so there aren’t actually 400 individual tools. Plus, don’t just assume that a 400-piece set will have what you need—before buying, check the product’s parts listing, usually found on the manufacturer’s website.

    Also, a helpful standard to remember is that the more parts in the set, the higher the price of the set. If you’re only going to use 100 of the 400 pieces, maybe opt for a smaller set of only the must-have mechanic tools.

    Industry observers note that mechanic tool sets can have a large number of accessories and adapters, including screwdriver bits, sockets, universal joint adapters, or breaker bars. The accessories and adapters included with a kit can vary widely and should be itemized on the parts list.

    Industry observers note that standard mechanic tool sets will come with basic accessories and adapters, including hex keys, extender bars, sockets, and screwdriver bits. For more specialized adapters, like a breaker bar or a torque wrench, you may need a larger set.

    According to recent reports, purchasing a large number of tools at once is an investment, so it’s important to be confident that the tools will work as expected. The best mechanic tools usually come with a warranty in case the product does not end up being as advertised.

    Check the manufacturer’s website or the seller’s product information to determine if there is a warranty on the tool set and to find out the details of the warranty.

    It has been revealed that the case that holds the pieces of the tool set should be of the same high quality as the tools inside. It’s not fun paying a premium price for high-end tools in a poor-quality case.

    The tools should fit neatly into designated areas within the case, making it easy for you to retrieve a specific tool. The tools should fasten tightly enough within their positions so as not to fall when the case is closed. This includes more difficult-to-store items, like sockets.

    Recent findings suggest that ideally, a storage case will be sturdy enough to withstand impact on a jobsite or in a vehicle without breaking or scattering the parts inside the case. Both metal and durable plastic are good options, with metal being a tougher exterior option and plastic weighing less for easier transportation.

    There are many advantages to owning a mechanic tool set, chief among them being the variety and included organization.

    Recent findings suggest that the variety of tools in a standard auto tool kit alone is enough to warrant purchasing a mechanic tool set. A mechanic tool set can include a significant range of options for power, convenience, or access to tight spaces. While some tool sets are costlier than others, a higher price tag may be reasonable when you consider that some sets have more than 300 tools, enough to outfit a user for many common DIY projects. Whether you’re changing an electrical outlet, installing a thermostat, or replacing your brake pads, a large good-quality set will provide you with everything you need without the inconvenience of having to buy each individual tool.

    Recent findings suggest that A mechanics tool set almost always comes with a handy carrying and storage case, keeping the tools neat and orderly plus easy to find, transport, and store as a tool collection grows. Don’t worry about losing your tools anymore; just place them back into their designated spot in the carrying case, and they’ll rest safely until you need them again. The case is also handy for transporting the tools from home to the worksite and back, or just carrying them from the shed to wherever you’re working on the house.

    The best mechanic tool set will typically include a few essential tools, including a hammer, tape measure, screwdrivers, ratchet and socket sets, as well as a wrench set, pliers, and a pry bar. Mechanics use quality tools both for professional use and to complete their own automotive repairs.

    Unfortunately, cars can break down while you are driving, so it’s a good idea to invest in a small mechanic tool set with some essentials for handling minor problems. Keep screwdrivers, pliers, adjustable wrenches, and sockets available in this mechanic tool kit, but it’s wise to also pack jumper cables, a jack, a tire iron, a spare tire, and a 12-volt air compressor so that you are well equipped in case of an emergency.

    Industry News: How to Shovel the Trickiest Surfaces the Right Way, From Pavers to Your Roof

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1191 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Familyhandyman

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • From lawns to sealed concrete, you might be surprised at how much damage a snow shovel can do.
    • Industry observers note that clearing snow from walkways is vital for safety, but winter shoveling can easily damage wooden decks, asphalt driveways and other surfaces.
    • According to recent reports, “Snow can camouflage uneven areas and patches of ice, posing slip-and-fall risks, particularly when you’re rushing to shovel,” notes landscaping expert Jose Lopez.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Family Handyman's Editorial Process.

    From lawns to sealed concrete, you might be surprised at how much damage a snow shovel can do.

    Industry observers note that clearing snow from walkways is vital for safety, but winter shoveling can easily damage wooden decks, asphalt driveways and other surfaces. So, as the days get shorter and colder, it’s key to solidify your shoveling plan before the first snow flies.

    According to recent reports, “Snow can camouflage uneven areas and patches of ice, posing slip-and-fall risks, particularly when you’re rushing to shovel,” notes landscaping expert Jose Lopez. “Being mindful and taking a relaxed, careful approach will help you save money and keep everyone safe all winter long.”.

    Ahead, experts walk through how to shovel eleven tricky surfaces around your home, to keep everyone safe, plus prevent costly springtime repairs.

    Sources indicate that shoveling gravel is frustrating because those pebbles tend to come up with the snow, then get scattered onto the landscaping. “You will end up cleaning about $150 worth of it off your lawn in the spring,” indicates grading and paving contractor Scott Flores.

    Industry observers note that to make life easier, use a plastic shovel, keep the blade about an inch above the gravel and clear the snow in short passes. “You don’t have to expose all of the gravel,” claims Lopez. “It’s fine to leave a thin layer of snow behind.”.

    A metal snow shovel blade can actually scratch and gouge concrete. “It can cause $3,000 worth of damage to your pavement in 20 minutes and you won’t know it ’til April,” says Flores. Initially, the damage “may not look like much, but once water gets under it and freezes, it will cause spalling and make your pavement look 10 years older than it is.”.

    Luckily, the fix is easy on this one: always use a poly-blade (plastic) or rubber-edged shovel on concrete.

    Aliaksandr Bahdanovich/Getty Images.

    Aggressive shoveling can damage paint and sealers, even if they’re touted as “scratch-resistant.” “That layer is about three millimeters thick, and your steel shovel will chip it away like you’re peeling your fingernails,” says Flores.

    The fix: use a poly-blade shovel, shovel with a slight upward motion and leave a half-inch of snow for the sun to melt, claims Flores. “Many believe that steel shovels will last longer. Yes they will, but that’s what makes them bad,” he says.

    Pro-tip: If you use a deicer, make sure it’s safe for your particular coating, says Lopez.

    It has been revealed that just like with concrete, asphalt seems indestructible, but metal shovels can damage it, especially if it already has imperfections or cracks. So, the best approach is to use a poly-blade (plastic) or rubber-edged shovel, and shovel the snow before it partially melts and refreezes.

    “Avoid pushing your shovel into cracks or potholes, and don’t bang it against the surface in an attempt to dislodge stubborn ice,” indicates Lopez. “Instead, choose a deicing product that’s safe for asphalt.”.

    Industry observers note that A shovel can easily catch the edge of a paver and scratch, break or knock it out of place. To prevent that, use a poly-blade shovel, take shorter shovel strokes, push snow at an angle and slightly raise up the leading edge.

    “Shoveling and deicing aggressively won’t make your job faster or easier, it takes some finesse,” claims Lopez. Also, use de-icers that are safe for both the paving and jointing material, and inspect the walkway for loose bricks once the snow melts.

    Recent findings suggest that after a snow, it can be tricky to tell where the concrete ends and the lawn begins, and one wrong move means damaged grass come springtime. To keep from marring your grass, mark walkway edges with small flags before it snows. While shoveling, keep the blade even with your walkway, versus angling it toward the grass.

    Pro-tip: “Slow down and work in short passes near the edges, rather than trying to force the shovel along,” says Lopez. “.

    Industry observers note that try not to pile snow on shrubs and other perennials, as that can snap branches. It’s also best to keep deicers and their runoff away from landscaping.

    Recent findings suggest that “Before winter arrives, plan where you’ll pile or toss snow to keep it away from sensitive plants,” claims Lopez. “You may find it helpful to use a smaller shovel, which will give you better control over where the snow lands.”.

    In a recent development, also, try not to move soil, which can expose plants to the cold, and never strike frozen branches to remove snow. “Wood breaks more easily than people expect,” says moving professional Leon Schwab.

    According to recent reports, aggressive shoveling is sure to damage a deck, regardless of its composition. To preserve yours, use a poly-blade shovel and push the snow in the direction of the boards. If it’s safe to do so, leave a thin layer of snow, instead of shoveling all the way down to bare decking, then apply a deicer that’s recommended for the surface type.

    Safety tip: “If wet, heavy snow is accumulating and you notice the deck sagging or hear creaking noises, seek professional advice,” says Lopez. “Don’t continue using the deck if you suspect a structural issue.”.

    Stairs are particularly hazardous when its slippery out, and clearing them can be precarious, with snow obscuring their boundaries and confined spaces limiting your range of motion.

    Industry observers note that to stay safe, “Wear boots with good traction and make sure your staircase is well lit,” states Lopez. “Don’t rush the job. It’s better to take your time and shovel safely.”.

    Pro-tip: “Use a small shovel to clear one step at a time and maintain a stable position,” notes Schwab.

    In a recent development, sometimes it’s prudent to clear large accumulations of snow from the roof, but it’s also a dangerous job. To stay safe, roofing contractor Andre Kazimierski recommends using a roof rake, which allows you to pull off snow while remaining on the ground. Focus on clearing off as much as you can, but don’t worry about leaving it completely bare, and try not to touch your roofing material.

    Recent findings suggest that “Do this sooner rather than later, because if it starts to warm up a bit the snow will become denser and heavier, making it harder to remove,” says Kazimierski. “And never walk on your roof when it’s even the slightest bit snowy or icy up there.”.

    Obviously, you don’t want to take a shovel to your car, as that would do a lot of damage. Instead, use a snow brush or broom that’s designed to be gentle on vehicle finishes. Flores recommends this one from Snow Joe.

    It has been revealed that start by clearing the roof in sections, then move on to the hood, trunk, windows, headlights, taillights and mirrors. You’ll especially want to get the roof and hood fully clear; otherwise, once you start driving, snow can blow up or slide down onto your windshield, obstructing your vision and endangering other drivers. “That ice can fly off your car at 40 miles per hour,” says Flores.

    How to Clean a Furnace

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1701 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Bobvila

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, we may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs.
    • Recent findings suggest that don’t wait until temperatures plummet to perform basic electric and gas furnace maintenance and cleaning.
    • The following steps can help you learn how to clean a furnace and keep the unit in tip-top shape throughout the winter.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, we may earn revenue from the products available on this page and participate in affiliate programs. Learn More ›.

    Recent findings suggest that don’t wait until temperatures plummet to perform basic electric and gas furnace maintenance and cleaning. By performing basic furnace cleaning and maintenance tasks now, you can avoid the expensive inconvenience (and danger) of leaving your family without heat during the coldest part of the year. You can also actually prolong the life of your furnace and coax it into operating at maximum energy efficiency.

    The following steps can help you learn how to clean a furnace and keep the unit in tip-top shape throughout the winter.

    There are several reasons why it’s necessary for a homeowner to either know how to clean a gas furnace or know when to schedule a professional cleaning with an HVAC expert. However, the most important reason is that regular cleaning and maintenance help to extend the life of a furnace and HVAC system, while reducing the number of costly repairs and breakdowns.

    Most system failures stem from dirt and dust choking out vital parts like the burners and flame sensors. Learning simple cleaning tasks, like how to clean a flame sensor on a furnace or how to clean the burners, prevents small complications from turning into expensive emergency repairs. Routine removal of soot, dirt, and dander as part of a furnace tune-up reduces wear and tear on internal components, helping the unit last its full 10- to 15-year expected lifespan.

    If you still aren’t sure this is a necessary part of HVAC maintenance, check out this list of additional reasons for why it’s best to clean your furnace.

    Bobvila.com may earn a commission from purchases made through these links.

    Sources indicate that most common furnace maintenance is not complicated—you just have to have a good vacuum cleaner and some basic tools and supplies. However, you do need to take a few precautions, so make sure to read and follow these steps in order to avoid skipping any important safety measures.

    According to recent reports, always turn off the electrical power and fuel supply before you start any furnace project. You can turn off the electricity by either toggling the on-off switch on the unit or turning off the breaker in your breaker panel.

    In a recent development, in order to turn off the gas, locate the fuel shutoff valve. The location of the valve varies depending on whether you have an oil or a gas furnace. The valve should either be near the oil tank for an oil furnace or on the incoming gas pipe for a gas furnace. After you locate it, turn the valve off.

    Industry observers note that wait several minutes to allow hot components to cool down before opening any panels. While you wait, use a microfiber cleaning cloth to wipe down the exterior of the furnace.

    With a screwdriver, unscrew and remove the upper and lower service panels to gain access to the interior cavity of the furnace.

    Sources indicate that the Ridgid vac has a 7-foot heavy-duty locking hose and a 15-foot cord and made quick work of both wet and dry messes in our tests. Read the review.

    Locate the small metal flame sensor rod near the burner assembly (often marked with a red or white connector). Unscrew and carefully pull the sensor out. Then gently scrub away soot or white-gray oxidation using fine-grit sandpaper or a wire brush until the metal shines. When you are done, wipe it clean and screw it back in.

    Sources indicate that basic furnace filters are designed to trap dust, dirt, and airborne particulates before they can enter the furnace and potentially damage its components. As filters become full, they become unable to filter the air. While some filters can be cleaned, while others need to be replaced. During the heating season, clean or replace the furnace filter every 1 to 3 months.

    It has been revealed that detach the burner cover and carefully slide or lift the burners out if they appear dirty or rusty. Brush any surface debris away with a soft-bristle brush or wash them in warm soapy water. After washing, rinse the burners thoroughly and dry them completely with compressed air before reinstalling.

    Inspect the blower wheel fins for heavy dust buildup with a flashlight or your phone camera. If you see dust, use your vacuum to clean loose dust from the fins using a brush attachment. However, when the blower wheel is heavily caked in grime, it’s best to call a technician for a deep wash. It isn’t recommended for an inexperienced DIYer to remove the blower, so it’s best to stick to light vacuuming and dusting for this part of the process.

    According to recent reports, put all access panels and doors back into place, ensuring any safety door switches are properly depressed, then turn the gas valve back on (parallel to the pipe) and restore power at the breaker or switch. Set your thermostat to Heat and watch to make sure the igniter glows, the gas catches smoothly into clean blue flames, and the blower kicks on.

    Recent findings suggest that ideally, you should clean the furnace once a year to keep it in top condition before the fall heating season begins. It also is a good idea to perform a quick clean in the spring, vacuuming up any dust or soot. Proper care and maintenance will help prolong the life of your furnace, and keep it running at peak efficiency.

    It has been revealed that plan to replace or clean your furnace air filters every 1 to 3 months, clean the furnace about once a year in the spring, and hire a pro to inspect and deep clean it every fall. Also, consider having your home’s air ductwork cleaned every 3 to 5 years.

    Although basic furnace maintenance can be handled by most homeowners, it makes sense to hire a professional for some tasks. For example, if you’ve noticed the furnace rumbling and can’t figure out why, then it’s best to call a pro for some on-site troubleshooting.

    Additionally, there are some cleaning jobs that should be left to the experts, so instead of trying to figure out how to clean a furnace heat exchanger, remove a blower, or clean the coils, it’s better to book a deep furnace cleaning with a trained furnace technician. Save yourself some time and potential problems by calling an HVAC pro for any of the following issues.

    It has been revealed that your furnace is a major investment in your home and your family’s comfort and safety. Regular cleaning and maintenance can save you money in the long run, because it will maximize the effective lifespan of your unit. Whether you are looking to maximize the efficiency and performance of a new or existing unit, just a couple of hours of cleaning and maintenance every year will help keep your investment in tip-top shape and make sure your family stays comfy and cozy during the colder winter months.

    Cleaning, changing filters, and lubricating your furnace are fairly simple steps in a process that really doesn’t take long. For a first-timer, it might take a few hours, since you might be dealing with unfamiliar equipment. After you have done it a few times, however, a full furnace clean should only take 1 to 2 hours. Changing the filters is even faster, and it only takes a few minutes to ensure that your air is clean and filtered.

    You should clean or service your furnace when you notice weak airflow, strange smells, or a spike in your energy bills. Here are other common signs that you should clean your furnace: • The furnace turns on and off rapidly when there are dirty flame sensors, clogged filters, or blocked burners that cause the unit to overheat.• Banging, screeching, or rattling sounds can mean the blower wheel is caked in debris or motor bearings need attention.• If dust settles swiftly around your furniture or return grilles soon after cleaning, your filter or blower compartment is likely overloaded.• The burner flame should burn steady and blue. A yellow flame means poor combustion and possible soot or carbon monoxide buildup.• An increase in sneezing, congestion, or dust-related irritation when the heat runs means the system is circulating allergens instead of trapping them.

    According to recent reports, failing to clean your furnace can lead to carbon monoxide leaks, higher energy bills, and system breakdowns. Dirt and soot can cause incomplete combustion or crack the heat exchanger, releasing invisible, odorless, and deadly carbon monoxide gas into your home.Thick accumulations of dust, lint, and debris near the burners, wiring, or moving components can overheat and spark an electrical or mechanical fire. Also, a dirty filter or blocked flame sensor can cause the furnace to repeatedly turn on and off in short bursts, failing to heat your home evenly. Additionally, clogged air filters and dirty internal parts block airflow, forcing the system to work harder and consume more fuel or electricity to heat your space. Neglected filters stop trapping dust, pollen, pet hair, and allergens, which then circulate through your vents and trigger asthma or allergy symptoms. All of this added strain wears out the blower motor, flame sensor, and other mechanical parts much faster, significantly cutting down the typical 15- to 20-year lifespan of a furnace.

    It has been revealed that the average cost to clean a furnace ranges from about $70 to $400, depending on the type and location of your furnace. Typically, oil furnaces will cost more since they require deeper cleaning, and any units located in the attic or crawlspace will naturally cost more due to the difficulty accessing these areas.

    An air humidifier and purifier puts two indoor-air appliances together into one space-saving everyday essential, filtering airborne pollutants while adding moisture when it gets too dry. We hands-on tested six combination models for two months, using them throughout bedrooms, offices, kitchens, and living spaces to compare purification, humidification, noise, controls, cleaning, and everyday usability.

    Our favorite is the Blueair 2-in-1 Purify+Humidify, which strikes the best balance of powerful performance and astonishingly thoughtful design. Its clean interface, polished app, hidden water reservoir, and understated styling also make it unusually pleasant to live with.

    Sources indicate that there are worthwhile options at much lower and much higher prices, though. From a roughly $100 Airthereal to Dyson’s feature-packed flagship, our testing revealed clear differences in value, noise, sensor responsiveness, and usability. Here are the best air humidifiers and purifiers we tested.

    Our top picks are among the best air humidifiers and purifiers for cleaner, more comfortable air at home. Plus, we hands-on tested some of these selected picks and included our testing results below.

    Blueair has consistently impressed us with its air-care products, and the 2-in-1 Purify+Humidify might be one of the brand’s most complete designs yet. Setup took almost no effort, and both the physical interface and Blueair app immediately stood out for being thoughtfully designed without feeling unnecessarily complicated. The controls are modern and elegant but still obvious enough that anyone can walk up and use them without consulting a manual.

    It has been revealed that the physical design is equally impressive. The water reservoir slides neatly out of sight, preserving the unit’s clean appearance, and we found refilling and cleaning it straightforward throughout two months of testing. That’s notable for an appliance that may live permanently in a bedroom or main living area. Unlike plenty of air-treatment equipment, this is something we don’t mind leaving on display.

    Performance sealed its Best Overall win. At normal speeds, it’s remarkably quiet; several times, we had to check that it was actually running. When our cooking degraded the surrounding air quality, though, the purifier immediately sprang into action and moved a serious amount of air. That naturally makes it much louder, but we’d rather hear the fan temporarily working hard than wait around for pollutants to clear. Overall, few models we tested balanced performance, usability, noise, and aesthetics this well.

    Industry observers note that what our tester says: “What impressed me most was how effortlessly this blended into everyday life. It’s super quiet, simple to use, easy to maintain, and good-looking enough that I never wanted to hide it.”—Paul Rankin, Product Reviews tester and writer.

    Get the Blueair humidifier and purifier at Amazon, Target, or Blueair.

    The Airthereal is considerably simpler than our premium picks, but that’s also why we like it. For around the $100 mark, it handles the core jobs well without feeling like a bargain-bin appliance. We ran it in an office for two months, where it quietly maintained a comfortable amount of humidity for me and several plants without turning the room into a rainforest.

    According to recent reports, one unexpectedly useful feature is the temperature readout on the display. Our test office tends to heat up after a desktop computer has been running all day, so being able to glance at the purifier for a quick room-temperature check became surprisingly handy. The upper humidifier portion also lifts off easily for refilling and cleaning, and the overall fit and finish look considerably more premium than the price suggests.

    In a recent development, what you’re paying for becomes obvious when you start using it. More impressively, the Dyson doesn’t just notice that the air has changed; it identifies what it’s detecting. During testing, even relatively small air-quality changes registered quickly, making the sensing system feel substantially more sophisticated than those on cheaper machines. Add its humidifying and fan functionality, extensive controls, and familiar Dyson engineering, and there’s a lot happening inside this appliance.

    According to recent reports, it’s also one of those rare pieces of household equipment we’d intentionally put somewhere visible. The PH2 looks more like a modern sculpture than an appliance that needs hiding in a corner. None of that changes the fact that the price is enormous, and shoppers who simply want cleaner, more comfortable air don’t need to spend this much. But for buyers who want advanced monitoring, premium design, and as much air-treatment technology as possible in one machine, nothing else we tested came close.

    Sources indicate that the Hunter HPH625 proves that an air purifier and humidifier doesn’t need to look clinical or overly technical. Its slim, modern shape works especially well in a bedroom, and Hunter offers several color options rather than the usual choice between white and slightly different white. We tested the dark green (sage) version, which looked particularly good in our guest bedroom and ultimately stayed there after testing ended.

    Day-to-day upkeep is equally bedroom-friendly. The reservoir is simple to refill, cleaning hasn’t been complicated, and automatic humidity sensing allows the machine to largely look after itself. We could set the desired conditions and leave it alone until it needed water or routine maintenance. For us, the most useful smart features are automatic operation and maintenance alerts rather than constant remote control. The InvisiClean isn’t the prettiest or fanciest model here, but its small footprint, quiet performance, and simplicity make it a practical compact choice.

    We tested six air purifier and humidifier combinations for two months throughout a home, placing them in bedrooms, an office, a kitchen, and larger shared living areas. One model, the Blueair 2-in-1 Pro, had already been in long-term use for more than a year and was retested alongside the newer machines.

    It has been revealed that we evaluated setup, controls and apps, humidification, purification response, noise, cleaning and refilling, and overall day-to-day usability. We also paid particular attention to automatic operation, noting how quickly each purifier responded when activities such as cooking or burning a candle changed surrounding air conditions. Since these are appliances many people leave visible and running continuously, design, reservoir access, maintenance, and how intrusive each unit felt during ordinary use also factored heavily into our scores and final awards.

    Living with dry and unclean air can negatively affect comfort and health. Dry indoor air can cause an uncomfortable feeling at best and cracked skin at worst. Even “clean” indoor air can benefit from an air purifier, which can remove common pollutants such as pollen, pet hair, and smoke. Air purifying is even more vital for allergy and asthma sufferers, who may notice a reduction in symptoms with a good air purifier.

    It has been revealed that there is a difference between air purifier and humidifier units: Purifiers remove pollutants from air, whereas humidifiers add moisture to the air. Combination units do both. Consider the following factors when shopping for the best air humidifier and purifier: room size, filtration system, reservoir capacity, and additional user-friendly features.

    Air humidifier and purifier combo units are intended for use in one room. (Whole-house humidifier and air purifier options are separate products and are usually professionally installed into the home’s climate control system.) For optimal performance, a unit should most often be used in a room that is the size of the manufacturer’s recommendation.

    It’s possible to use a unit rated for a larger room in a smaller room, however, as long as a unit has a humidistat and auto-shutoff. The humidistat measures the ideal humidity, usually between 30 and 50 percent, and triggers the unit to shut off when ideal humidity is reached. Just know that if there’s no auto shut-off feature, a large humidifier can make a small room too humid.

    While it’s notable to take room size into account, the recommended room size can sometimes be misleading, so consider the CADR rating as well, explained ahead.

    It has been revealed that air humidifiers and purifiers can have a few filter types, and many have a multistage filtration system. These systems can include activated carbon filters to remove odors, large particle filters, dust and pet hair filters, and the “gold standard,” HEPA (high-efficiency particulate air) filters. HEPA filters remove over 99.97 percent of dust mites, mold, pollen, bacteria, and other airborne particles measuring 0.3 microns (and actually trap smaller and larger particles even more effectively).

    These extremely effective humidifiers with filters are shown to improve air quality. Shoppers who are interested in an air purifier and humidifier for allergies will want to look for a unit with a HEPA filter.

    Sources indicate that air humidifiers and purifiers have a CADR (clean air delivery rate) score. This rating is used to measure an air purifier’s efficiency. It indicates the amount of filtered air a unit can deliver per minute and is often broken down into separate ratings for tobacco smoke, dust, and pollen. Products certified by the AHAM (Association of Home Appliance Manufacturers) are proven to live up to their CADR rating.

    It has been revealed that the higher the CADR score, the faster the filtration system. CADR is often used to calculate the appropriate square footage for a unit. The AHAM recommends that the CADR score of a unit should be a minimum of two-thirds of the room’s square footage.

    Some units don’t display a CADR score and only display the room size the unit is suitable for. Knowing the CADR score is more reliable, as some manufacturers will recommend a room size that does not align with the AHAM’s recommendations. According to the AHAM, the recommended room size should be based on 4.8 air changes per hour (how many times the purifier cleans and circulates the air in a room). Many manufacturers will share a recommended room size based on only one or two air changes per hour to boost their square footage recommendation.

    Air humidifier purifier units have a reservoir to hold water, which the machine turns into moisture to release into the air. The unit’s overall size (and therefore reservoir size) often corresponds to its suited room size. Small units are usually ideal for small or medium-size rooms, but they may need more frequent refilling if they also have a small reservoir tank. Larger units will need less frequent topping up, but they’ll also take up more space.

    Keep in mind that usage habits will also affect how often the water tank needs refilling. Many air humidifiers and purifiers have a water tank between a half gallon and 1 gallon, but extra-large options are also available—we’ve included one with a 3-gallon-plus capacity on this list.

    According to recent reports, in our testing, reservoir design mattered almost as much as capacity. A slightly smaller tank that’s easy to remove, carry, and clean can be less frustrating than a larger reservoir with awkward access.

    Daily cleaning and maintenance can ensure that your air cleaner humidifier operates correctly and does not emit any harmful particles into a space. Customers are encouraged to use distilled water in their humidifiers and purifiers to reduce general maintenance and germ buildup. Wash and dry the humidifier after each use to remove any potential bacteria, mold, minerals, and chemicals.

    The Environmental Protection Agency advises using a 3 percent hydrogen peroxide solution to clean these machines every few days, clearing out any potential toxins. Finally, filters should be replaced as recommended by the manufacturer to ensure all contaminants are being removed.

    It has been revealed that A good air humidifier and purifier should have a built-in humidistat that measures room humidity and adjusts operation accordingly. At minimum, the humidifier should shut off once the set humidity is reached to prevent the room from becoming overly damp.

    Digital onboard controls are also useful, especially when they make it easy to adjust fan speed, humidity targets, and operating modes. Some models include a remote control for making changes from across the room.

    It has been revealed that smart models can connect to Wi-Fi and a smartphone app for monitoring air quality, setting schedules, and changing settings remotely. In our testing, however, we often found the physical controls faster for everyday adjustments. Apps were most useful for checking air-quality data and receiving maintenance alerts.

    Filter-change and refill reminders are particularly helpful, whether they appear in an app or through indicator lights on the unit itself.

    Industry observers note that choosing the best air humidifier and purifier for your home really comes down to choosing a user-friendly option that’s suitable for the intended room size. Still wondering if a combined purifier and humidifier is the right choice? Read on for some frequently asked questions and answers on room air purifiers and humidifiers to narrow down the best option for your needs.

    No, air purifiers do not dry out a space’s air supply, especially when the machine includes a humidifier. These machines are designed to improve indoor air quality by removing particles, microorganisms, and gases.

    No—air purifiers trap mold and common allergen particles in the air, but not the mold spores that may be present somewhere in the home. To completely get rid of a mold problem, consider an effective mold remover.

    It has been revealed that yes. Air purifiers and humidifiers perform different functions, so they can be used at the same time without interfering with each other. An air purifier filters airborne pollutants, while a humidifier adds moisture to dry air. In fact, combination units like the ones we tested are specifically designed to perform both jobs from the same location. Just avoid over-humidifying the room; aim to keep indoor humidity between about 30 and 50 percent.

    Sources indicate that yes. Air purifiers are designed to be left on at all times. In fact, running an air purifier as often as possible is the most effective way to improve air quality. After all, indoor air quality is always changing depending on the air quality outside and what you do inside, like cooking, cleaning, or smoking. Leaving the air purifier on will help improve air quality, regardless of exterior factors.

    In a way, yes. Stand-alone humidifiers don’t remove pollutants, but they do improve overall air quality by making the air feel more comfortable. Humidifiers can help keep indoor air humidity at an ideal level between 30 and 50 percent. Keeping indoor humidity in this sweet spot reduces the chance of mold growth and dust mites, which in turn can help maintain better air quality. To further improve air quality, look for a combined air purifier humidifier unit.

    Sources indicate that no, not necessarily. A humidifier is useful if you struggle with dry indoor air. It’s not necessary (and can even be detrimental) to run a humidifier in humid homes. If the air in your home often dips beneath 30 percent, consider using a humidifier.

    According to recent reports, the unit needs to run for a certain length of time for you to take full advantage of the air purifier and humidifier benefits. Effectiveness depends on a wide range of factors, including the room size, the air purifier’s filtration system, the unit’s settings, and the surrounding humidity level. Consider the CADR rating and recommended room size to find a suitable unit. When these metrics are all taken into account, a good air purifier should create cleaner air in around just 15 minutes.
